key_insight: Bayesian inference on photoluminescence imaging can localize where perovskite solar cells degrade—at the hole/electron transport interfaces or in the bulk—while the device is operating and aging.
engineering_relevance: The method turns imaging data into spatially resolved diagnostics that can guide targeted passivation and more durable perovskite cell design.
method: Photoluminescence imaging of fully fabricated perovskite solar cells
Drift-diffusion simulations linked to measured optical data
Bayesian inference to infer spatial maps of recombination-related parameters
evidence_signal: The authors tracked inferred parameter maps during accelerated aging at 70 °C under full-spectrum sunlight and observed pronounced spatial heterogeneity, with the strongest degradation localized to perovskite/transport-layer interfaces.
watch_item: Because the approach depends on model-based inference from imaging, accuracy may be sensitive to simulation assumptions, parameter identifiability, and measurement quality.
paper_title: Disentangling the origin of degradation in perovskite solar cells via optical imaging and Bayesian inference
